style: Say warmly and clearly, like a friendly owl librarian giving young children a tour
lines: Picture books have lots of pictures and fewer words. Their spine labels start with E, for Everybody. They are in ABC order by the author's last name.
Fiction means made-up stories, like chapter books. Spine labels start with FIC, then the author's last name, in ABC order.
Nonfiction books are true. They teach facts about animals, space, people and places. They are in number order, and each number is a topic.
At the checkout desk, the librarian scans your book so you can take it home. Bring it back by the due date so others can read it too!
The reading rug is a cozy spot for story time and quiet reading. Use a soft voice so everyone can enjoy their book.
Hoo-hoo! Welcome to the library. Tap a part of the library to visit it.
That's a good place to read it! But where does it live on the shelves?
E is for Everybody: picture books.
A number on the spine means a true book.
Put the picture books in ABC order. Look at the letters on the spine!
The shelf is in ABC order. Now anyone can find these books!
